title: Funding and acquisitions in Indian startups this week [Aug 31 - Sep 05]
summary:
This week, 25 Indian startups raised $303.7 million across five growth-stage deals, 16 early-stage deals and three undisclosed rounds. The week also saw seven key hires, four mergers and acquisitions, two startup shutdowns and 250 layoffs.

In contrast, 24 startups had collectively secured about $218.7 million in the previous week.
[Growth-stage deals]
Growth-stage startups raised $201.9 million across five deals this week. Digital banking startup Slice led the funding with a $100 million round at a $450 million valuation, led by Neo Wealth with participation from Kado Global, Moore Strategic Ventures and Raise Financial.
Wearable tech startup Ultrahuman has raised $70 million in a round led by Qualcomm Ventures, with participation from Labcorp, Alpha Wave, Blume Ventures, Nexus Venture Partners, Alteria and other investors. D2C skincare brand SUGAR Cosmetics has raised Rs 144.5 crore ($15.2 million) from existing investor A91 Partners at a valuation of Rs 755 crore, down 75% from its last valuation of Rs 3,000 crore.
Homegrown sneaker brand Comet has raised around Rs 100 crore in its Series B round led by Belgium-based investment firm Verlinvest. Pune-based deeptech company Aeron Systems has raised Rs 45 crore ($4.7 million) in a Pre-Series B funding round
[Early-stage deals]
Early-stage startups raised $101.8 million across 16 deals this week. BaaS provider Yuma Energy raised $35 million in Series A funding led by Magna International, while NextGen Finance raised Rs 215 crore led by Beams Fintech Fund.
Consumer health startup Cradlewise raised $12 million in Series A funding led by 3one4 Capital and Prudent Investment Management. Space infrastructure startup Kepler Aerospace raised $8 million in seed funding led by Blue Ashva Capital.
Former Google AI lead Prashant Jalan launched Guickly with $4.2 million in seed funding led by Engineering Capital. Deeptech startup Zenergize Technologies also raised $4 million in Pre-Series A funding led by Giraffe Studios.
Other startups that raised funding this week included deeptech firms Zenergize Technologies, Minimac Systems and Alteon, along with indoor air-quality company YOGa Clean Air and six other startups. 
Voice-first AI tutoring platform YoLearn.ai, English learning app SpeakX, neurotechnology startup Neurotech and deeptech firm BQP also raised funding this week, with amounts undisclosed.
[City and segment-wise deals]
Bengaluru led the funding charts with 14 startup deals during the week, followed by Delhi-NCR with five. Mumbai, Pune and Hyderabad also recorded deals.

Deeptech startups led the sectors with five deals, followed by healthtech and AI with four deals each. E-commerce bagged 3 deals during the week while Fintech and edtech startups recorded two deals each, while e-commerce, EV, spacetech, manufacturing and other sectors also saw funding activity.
[Series-wise deals]
Series A rounds led the week with 8 deals, followed by Series A and pre-seed rounds with five  deals and four deals respectively. Series D, Series B, Pre-Series A, Series C  and pre-Series B also recorded one deal each during the week.

[Week-on-week funding trend]
On a weekly basis, startup funding surged over 39% to $303.7 million from $218.7 million raised in the previous week.
The average weekly funding over the past eight weeks stood at around $218.25 million across 20 deals.
[Key Hirings / Departures]
This week, Bengaluru-based digital healthcare platform MediBuddy appointed Shalabh Shrivastava as its Head of Operations to strengthen processes and technology-led execution. Fintech platform Pine Labs also appointed Jayaram Karthik, former SVP of Business Operations at Razorpay, as its chief operations officer.
Wingify has appointed Mehernaz Dalal as its chief financial officer. Boldfit has appointed former Lenskart chief business officer Oliver Kaye as its chief operating officer. Enterprise SaaS company Genefied has appointed Neha Lakhwara as Head of Investor Relations and Strategy. Technology-led credit inclusion platform BankSathi has appointed Nitish Kumar Bugalia as co-founder and chief operating officer.
[Mergers and Acquisitions]
Gurugram-based insurtech startups InsuranceDekho and RenewBuy have merged to create a unified pan-India insurance distribution platform under the InsuranceDekho brand, with founder and CEO Ankit Agrawal leading the combined entity. 
Bengaluru-based travel-fintech platform Niyo has agreed to acquire Capital India Finance’s forex and cross-border business, operated under the RemitX brand. The deal will bring RemitX’s branch network, distribution partners, employees and brand under Niyo.
Adobe has picked up India based marketing intelligence startup Rilo in a deal involving the licensing of its technology and acquisition of its team. This is Adobe’s second acquisition from India.
Cloud-based lending platform Lenra AI has acquired Israel-based data science company Data Harbor in an undisclosed deal. Founded by Ephraim Goldin, Data Harbor provides real-time data consolidation, predictive analytics and data science services, with the acquisition aimed at strengthening Lenra’s Intelligence Stack and automation across the lending lifecycle.
[Layoffs]
Uber is set to lay off around 200-250 employees in India as part of a global restructuring, with cuts expected across its People and Earners teams, according to an ET report. Globally, the company is eliminating around 3,300 roles, or 10% of its workforce, in its largest workforce reduction since the Covid-19 pandemic.
Eternal, the parent company of Zomato and Blinkit, is set to lay off around 250 employees as part of a restructuring of its customer support operations.
[Shutdown]
Gurugram-based e-grocery startup Satvacart has shut down after 12 years, with August 28 marking its last day of operations. The shutdown follows years of funding challenges, with smaller capital tranches proving insufficient to rebuild and scale the business.

Unified Payments Interface (UPI) recorded its highest-ever monthly transaction volume in August 2026, processing 24.51 billion transactions worth Rs 29.82 lakh crore, according to NPCI data. Transaction volume rose 3.6% MoM and 22% YoY, while transaction value declined 0.2% MoM but grew 20% YoY. UPI processed an average 791 million transactions worth Rs 96,205 crore daily during the month.
India’s electric two-wheeler industry recorded an 11% month-on-month decline in August to 1.82 lakh units from 2.05 lakh units in July, with most major players witnessing a steep drop. TVS Motor retained the top spot with 48,873 registrations and a 27.04% market share, despite a 12.45% MoM decline.
Indian new-age companies saw substantial secondary market activity in August, with 17 block and bulk deals worth Rs 26,337 crore ($2.77 billion) across 12 companies, including Lenskart, Groww, Meesho, Eternal and Paytm. The activity was largely driven by early-stage investors and promoters offloading their holdings, while mutual funds, insurers and global institutional investors emerged as key buyers.
CREW, the premium concierge platform from the Swiggy ecosystem, has entered the travel space with a dedicated personal travel concierge offering for avid travellers. The platform plans, books and curates journeys end to end, from discovery to on-site assistance. The move follows a year of learnings since CREW’s launch, with travel emerging as the category seeing the strongest demand for seamless, end-to-end convenience.
Swiggy and Hero MotoCorp have partnered to offer delivery partners exclusive pricing on Hero models, customised financing solutions with up to 90% LTV and competitive interest rates. The partnership will also provide road safety training under Hero MotoCorp’s Ride Safe India initiative, covering safe riding practices, traffic rules, hazard anticipation and emergency response.
India’s leading travel fintech platform has launched biometric authentication for UPI payments on Scapia Pay, allowing users to authenticate transactions below Rs 10,000 through a fingerprint or face scan instead of entering their bank-linked UPI PIN. Payments are verified using Face ID on iOS and fingerprint recognition on Android, making transactions faster and more secure.
MapmyIndia Mappls, in partnership with AI-driven data analytics firm ClarityX, has launched Geo-FI, a comprehensive geo-intelligence platform for lending. The platform integrates spatial insights into the lending process to help BFSI companies assess borrower risk and identify opportunities.
Edtech major Unacademy has been acquired by UpGrad for just over $200 million, marking a 94% decline from its peak valuation of around $3.4 billion in 2021. Unacademy cofounder and CEO Gaurav Munjal confirmed the deal, noting that the company had raised funds at its peak but is now being sold at a fraction of that valuation.

title: Sugar Cosmetics raises Rs 144 Cr at Rs 755 Cr valuation; early investors seek steep discount exits
summary:
Sugar Cosmetics, once among the better-known names in India’s D2C beauty wave, has raised Rs 144.5 crore from existing investor A91 Partners as the company faces continued pressure on revenue and profitability. The funding comes alongside efforts by some early investors to find buyers for their stakes at steep discounts to the company’s peak valuation.
The board approved the allotment of 1,12,248 Series CCPS at an issue price of Rs 12,871 per share to raise Rs 144.5 crore, according to regulatory filings. A91 Partners subscribed to the entire issue.
Based on the allotment and resulting shareholding, Entrackr estimates that the transaction values Sugar at around Rs 755 crore post-money, 75% below its peak valuation of around Rs 3,000 crore. A91 will hold around 19.97% in the company following the new round.
On Friday, ET reported that the firm was raising Rs 140-150 crore from A91 at a valuation of Rs 500-600 crore. 
The latest primary round is also taking place as some existing investors explore secondary exits. Sources said investors are looking to sell stakes worth up to Rs 150 crore. Some early backers have been approaching potential buyers at steep discounts to Sugar’s peak valuation.
Entrackr has also learnt that a consulting firm has been pitching Sugar shares at a fraction of its peak valuation, with a minimum transaction size of around Rs 25 crore. The discussions underline the extent of the valuation correction since the peak of the D2C funding cycle.
Sugar was valued at around $400 million, or roughly Rs 3,000 crore, in 2022 when it raised $50 million in a Series D round led by L Catterton. At the time, the company was expanding its offline retail footprint and had emerged as a prominent youth-focused cosmetics brand.
The business has since lost momentum. Sugar’s revenue declined 20% to Rs 404 crore in FY25 from Rs 505 crore in FY24, while its net loss almost doubled to Rs 135 crore from Rs 68 crore. 
Founded by Vineeta Singh and Kaushik Mukherjee, Sugar started as an online-first beauty brand before building a sizable offline presence. It sells makeup and personal care products through marketplaces, its own platform and a network of retail outlets.
The latest round paints a very different picture from Sugar’s 2022 fundraise. A91, which already held roughly a fifth of Sugar, is putting fresh capital into the company even as other investors look for exits at sharply lower valuations.
For Sugar, the funding provides capital to stabilise the business, but also marks a clear reset in investor expectations. It now needs to rebuild revenue, improve profitability and demonstrate stronger unit economics.
The reset, however, does not necessarily spell the end of Sugar’s growth story. Its brand recognition and distribution network give it room to recover if it can sharpen its product portfolio, improve economics and return to growth.
For early investors, the priority appears to have shifted from waiting for a large exit to finding liquidity at a fraction of Sugar’s earlier valuation. The latest round reflects how sharply expectations have changed, while leaving Sugar with the task of proving it can bounce back.

Existing investors Elevation Capital and Nexus Venture Partners also participated in the round. Angel investors including Urban Company cofounder Abhiraj Singh Bhal, Snap’s global chief business officer Ajit Mohan and Bhaane founder Anand Ahuja also joined the round.

Comet plans to use the fresh capital to accelerate retail expansion, product development and technology capabilities, along with investments in research and development. The company is also developing its own sole moulds and tooling for new footwear models.
Founded in 2023 by Utkarsh Gupta and Dishant Daryani, Bengaluru-based Comet currently has four footwear models and plans to double its portfolio to eight models by the end of next year. It is also preparing to launch a women-focused model backed by dedicated sole tooling.
The company has grown its revenue ninefold since its previous institutional fundraise and is set to reach 10 stores this month. It plans to expand its retail network to 20 stores by the end of FY27.
In FY25, Comet’s revenue rose nearly fourfold to Rs 29 crore, while its loss widened to Rs 4.39 crore. The company is yet to file its FY26 financials.

title: "I Shut Down Satvacart 45 Days Before Break-Even"
summary:
Orders had risen 2.5 times in two days and the contribution margin was positive. But the bank account was empty, investors had walked away and, after 12 years of absorbing every shock, I could absorb no more. A founder’s capacity is capital too
On August 28, 2026, I shut down Satvacart.
The decision came at a strange moment. Orders had risen 2.5 times in two days. The contribution margin was positive. Our calculations suggested we were roughly 45 days from break-even. After 12 years of rebuilding the company through funding droughts, operational breakdowns and multiple changes of model, the business was moving in the right direction.
I was not.
Our funds were at zero. Rain and waterlogging had disrupted deliveries. A delivery executive stopped reporting because his salary was unpaid, forcing us to use Porter. A $500,000 funding conversation had already collapsed. Then, on August 27, an investor considering a larger $3 million cheque backed out. The following day, our operations head called: a picker would not work beyond noon. Operations would have to stop.
None of these problems was new. I had solved some versions of each many times. On 11 occasions in 12 years, I had virtually no money in my pocket and none in the company’s bank account. Salaries had been delayed. Operations had stalled. Once, the situation escalated until I had to call the police. Each time, we found a way through.
This time, I could not find a responsible reason to ask employees to work unpaid for a few more days while I chased another investor for another small cheque. Satvacart did not close because customers had disappeared or because online grocery had become impossible. It closed because its founder had reached saturation.
That distinction matters. Startups measure runway in months of cash. They rarely measure how many shocks the founder can still absorb. Founder capacity is capital too, and mine had run out.
The business had not run out of juice
Satvacart began 12 years ago as one of Gurugram’s early online grocery businesses. We survived several funding meltdowns, rebuilt the company five times and demonstrated profitability at one stage. Transactions were still growing when I stopped.
Gurugram has roughly 10 lakh households and continues to grow rapidly. Even without meaningful marketing, we were seeing around 300 app launches and four first transactions a day. Our average order value was ₹950. Some loyal customers placed 15 to 30 orders a month. Our contribution margin had previously reached about ₹250 an order.
The plan was simple enough to fit on a napkin. Get back to 2,500 households, lift average frequency from four orders a month to seven and hold contribution margin at ₹250 an order. That would produce ₹43.75 lakh in monthly contribution margin. After roughly ₹10 lakh in fixed cluster costs, including marketing, one cluster could generate about ₹33.75 lakh in monthly EBIT.
Then replicate the cluster. Internal cash generation, not endless fundraising, would finance expansion. The dot-com crash, the Lehman crisis and Covid had all delivered the same warning: external capital can disappear overnight.
The model was not fantasy. We had made it profitable before. What we never completed was the replication. In grocery, a profitable store is evidence; a profitable network is the company. We proved the first and ran out of capital and founder capacity before proving the second.
What 12 years taught me about capital
My first fundraising mistake was almost comical. I told an investor I needed ₹25 lakh because that was what my spreadsheet said would take us to profitability. I had budgeted for the plan, not for reality. The seed round eventually became ₹86 lakh.
A founder should not raise enough for everything to go right. The money must cover suppliers, salaries, technology, experiments, failed campaigns, delayed fundraising and the things nobody had the imagination to predict. Once a business has paying customers, I now believe a seed round of around $2 million is often the minimum required to reach the next independently fundable milestone. Anything smaller can leave the company perpetually fundraising and dangerously distracted.
More money, however, is not permission to become careless. We developed a small ritual: no payments for 48 hours after investor funds hit the bank. The pause prevented the psychological release of finally seeing money from turning into instant spending.
Undercapitalisation also distorts behaviour. Towards the end, we were raising ₹7 lakh, ₹2 lakh, ₹3 lakh and ₹5 lakh at a time, sometimes through deeply discounted rounds. Satvacart had more than 125 shareholders and another 340 CSOP subscribers through Tyke. If half the shareholders had put in ₹2 lakh each, we could have raised about ₹1.25 crore, enough to take the business to profitability. Most had stopped answering calls and messages. A few continued to help, but cheques of ₹50,000 or ₹1 lakh bought days, not a future.
Small cheques can keep a company alive while quietly preventing it from confronting whether it has a fundable path. Survival and progress are not the same thing.
Growth can lie
The grocery business taught me to distrust growth when it is separated from unit economics.
Take a ₹10 packet of Parle-G to a neighbourhood kirana and offer the shopkeeper ₹5. He will refuse because he understands the transaction immediately: selling a ₹10 product for ₹5 destroys value. A startup can sell the same packet for ₹2.50, classify the ₹7.50 loss as customer acquisition cost and celebrate the resulting spike in orders.
It has acquired a transaction. It may not have acquired a customer.
The distortion gets worse when companies showcase Net Order Value calculated using MRP multiplied by units sold instead of the price customers actually paid. A deeper discount can then create prettier growth. Activity rises, headlines improve and capital is raised, while the underlying economics deteriorate.
At Satvacart, contribution margin became the number I trusted. Revenue and orders matter only after a founder knows what each additional transaction contributes. Discounts can introduce a customer to a service. They cannot be the service.
Customer obsession also requires visibility, not slogans. In 2016, we built a simple post-delivery feedback system that allowed customers to write whatever they wanted. Nearly 90 per cent of our customers had my phone number, and I called many of them directly. The team knew poor service could reach me without travelling through layers of hierarchy.
Founders often treat systems as automation. The first job of a system is more basic: tell you that something is going wrong before it becomes a crisis. Capital can buy software and staff. It cannot compensate for a management team that has become blind to the doorstep.
Reduce the problem before expanding the dream
The most useful advice I received rarely sounded grand. Early on, I spent weeks trying to perfect the company’s name. Vijay, a friend and adviser, recognised the analysis paralysis and pushed me to launch. Years later, when others thought Satvacart should close, he came to the office and asked: ‘Do you want to survive, or do you want to shut down?’
I said I wanted to survive. He told me to surrender the office, remove non-essential staff and protect only the core operation.
Another adviser, Ujj Nath, shared the story of Subway narrowing its focus to one store when bankruptcy threatened. One store has fewer problems than 100. Make it work, understand why it works and only then multiply it.
Startup culture often mistakes a wider battlefield for greater ambition. Sometimes ambition means reducing the problem until it can be solved. Satvacart’s cluster plan came from that lesson. It was our attempt to turn one viable operating unit into a repeatable company.
The company must sometimes leave the founder’s head
The question that stalked me for 12 years was painfully simple: Kya hoga, kaise hoga? What will happen, and how will it happen?
No founder can answer it honestly every night. My former boss Rahul Rishi, a partner at EY, once told me that problems eventually get resolved if you keep trying. I learnt that the situation at 11 pm is not necessarily the situation at 11 am. Make one more call. Solve the next problem. Stay alive long enough for circumstances to change.
Spirituality helped me live with what could not be solved that night. The lesson I took from the Bhagavad Gita was to work on the duty in front of me without pretending I controlled the future. Glenn Harrold’s deep-sleep recordings helped quieten the loops of overthinking. Neither is a prescription. Every founder needs a method that allows the company to leave the head for a few hours. Without one, the business consumes the person expected to save it.
In Satvacart’s final days, we even built what I called an AI-led marketing organisation. ChatGPT acted as CMO, Codex as analyst and executor, Gemini worked on Google Ads and Meta AI on Facebook campaigns. I made the final decisions. Orders jumped 2.5 times in two days while contribution margin stayed positive.
The machine was working. The founder was exhausted.
Closing Satvacart does not persuade me that online grocery has room for only two giants. It persuades me that a viable grocery company still needs sufficient capital, disciplined economics, systems that expose trouble early and a founder able to survive the distance between proof and scale.
We had customers. We had positive contribution. We had a route to break-even. What we no longer had was enough cash or human capacity to travel the final 45 days.
That is the hardest lesson I carry from Satvacart: a startup can remain alive on a spreadsheet after the person carrying it has reached the end.
By our guest author Rahul H. Saxena.
Rahul H. Saxena was the founder and CEO of Satvacart, an online grocery startup he built and ran for 12 years until its operations were discontinued in August 2026. Before founding Satvacart, he worked as a consultant at EY and held corporate strategy roles at Cleartrip, with experience spanning strategy, business transformation, data analytics and systems design. He also worked with O3 Capital and NetApp.

title: Cars24 revenue declines for second year in a row, core biz falls 23% in FY26
summary:
Cars24’s revenue continued to decline for the second consecutive year as the used-car marketplace navigated a challenging FY26 marked by cost cuts, layoffs and a series of senior-level exits.
The company’s revenue from operations fell 18.3% to Rs 5,092 crore in the fiscal year ended March 2026, from Rs 6,233 crore in FY25 and Rs 6,917 crore in FY24, according to its consolidated financial statements filed with the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

The sale of cars through its auction and retail businesses remained the biggest contributor, accounting for around 87% of operating revenue. However, revenue from this segment declined 22.7% to Rs 4,349 crore in FY26, pointing to stress in its core used-car business. The segment had already declined 11% in FY25, indicating that pressure on the core biz has persisted for a second consecutive year and weighed on overall scale.
The remaining operating income came from financial services, including interest on loans provided through its Loans24 platform, as well as service fees, parking fees, and other offerings such as insurance assistance and warranties. These collectively contributed around Rs 653 crore during the year.
Cars24 also recorded Rs 128 crore in other income, largely from interest on current deposits, taking its total income to Rs 5,220 crore, compared with Rs 6,358 crore in the previous fiscal year.
With the business shrinking, car procurement remained the company’s largest cost centre but fell 23.7% to Rs 4,212 crore. However, employee benefit expenses rose 33.4% to Rs 806 crore, while marketing expenses remained broadly stable at Rs 105 crore. In the end, Cars24’s overall expenses declined 17.7% to Rs 5,674 crore during the last fiscal year.
The company’s financial year also saw significant organisational changes. In April 2025, Cars24 laid off around 200 employees across functions as part of a restructuring exercise, with CEO Vikram Chopra saying some projects and roles had been added prematurely.
The leadership churn continued in 2026. India used-car CEO Himanshu Ratnoo stepped down in March, with Chopra taking direct oversight of the business. Co-founder Gajendra Jangid subsequently stepped back from day-to-day operations, while co-founder and COO Mehul Agrawal also exited his operating role in April.
Despite the decline in revenue, Cars24 narrowed its net loss by 18.8% to Rs 441 crore in FY26 from Rs 543 crore in FY25. Its EBITDA margin stood at 8.63%, while ROCE was 19.6% during the last fiscal year.
Spinny has emerged as the leading player in India’s used-car retail space, with revenue growing over 28% in FY26, unlike Cars24, which saw another year of decline. Spinny touched the Rs 6,000 crore revenue threshold in FY26 and is expected to grow 25-30% in FY27, according to sources. The company also raised $320 million over the past year, giving it more room to scale as Cars24 works to regain momentum.
For Cars24, the immediate priority is to restore growth in its used-car business before pursuing larger expansion plans. The company is also yet to complete its reverse flip from Singapore to India, adding another step before it can seriously prepare for a public listing.
With the IPO timeline no longer clearly in sight, Cars24 will need to demonstrate that its used-car retail and auction businesses can return to growth and support stronger economics. Until then, narrowing losses alone may not be enough to rebuild the scale and market confidence needed for a successful public-market push.

title: Flipkart Minutes’ order value nears Blinkit’s: UBS
summary:
Flipkart’s quick-commerce platform Minutes is seeing order values close to market leader Blinkit, with its mobile and electronics mix giving it an advantage in overall basket size, according to UBS.
Excluding mobile phones, Flipkart Minutes’ net order value stands at around Rs 500-530, slightly below Blinkit’s average net order value of Rs 518 as of Q1 FY27. However, when mobile phones are included, Minutes’ order value is higher than Blinkit’s, reflecting Flipkart’s established strength in mobiles and electronics.
The higher basket size could give Minutes an edge as it scales its quick commerce operations. While the platform initially had a higher mix of mobile orders, electronics and mobile categories have become a bigger contributor to its overall portfolio over the past year.
Flipkart’s expertise and existing seller relationships in mobiles and electronics have helped Minutes differentiate itself from other quick-commerce platforms. At the same time, the company is expanding Minutes’ fresh category alongside beauty, personal care and other immediate-use categories.
Minutes has now expanded to more than 1,000 dark stores across 120-130 cities. The all-India network averages around 800-1,000 orders per store per day, while mature stores can reach 1,200-1,500 orders per day within five to six months of launch.
Minutes’ advertising revenue is broadly comparable with other leading quick-commerce platforms, according to the UBS expert. Gross margins are improving but remain below Blinkit’s levels, while city-level economics are expected to improve as markets mature. Store and city maturity will remain important drivers of Minutes’ margin trajectory.
With order values nearing Blinkit’s levels, advertising revenue broadly in line with leading peers and a higher overall basket when mobile orders are included, Minutes’ category mix could remain an important differentiator as Flipkart expands its quick-commerce footprint.
Blinkit, meanwhile, continues to lead the quick-commerce market on user reach. Its share of tracked monthly active users stood at 38% in July, up 31 basis points month-on-month and 375 basis points year-on-year. summary:
Rentomojo, the Accel-backed furniture and appliance rental platform, has filed its Red Herring Prospectus (RHP) for its initial public offering (IPO).
The Bengaluru-based company is looking to raise around Rs 1,255.6 crore through the IPO, which will comprise a fresh issue of Rs 150 crore and an offer-for-sale (OFS) of around 2.73 crore shares worth Rs 1,105.6 crore.
The company has fixed a price band of Rs 384-404 per share, valuing Rentomojo at around Rs 4,200 crore at the upper end. The IPO will open for subscription on September 9 and close on September 11, while anchor investors can bid on September 8.
Existing investors, including Accel India, Edelweiss, IDG Ventures India, ValueQuest, Madison India and GMO, along with founder Geetansh Bamania, will sell shares through the OFS.
Rentomojo plans to use the fresh issue proceeds primarily to strengthen its balance sheet. About Rs 70 crore will go towards debt repayment, while another Rs 42.5 crore will be used for lease rentals and licence fees for its warehouses and experience stores.
According to the company’s DRHP, Accel India is the largest shareholder with a 20.92% stake, followed by founder Geetansh Bamania and Chiratae Ventures with 14.69% and 13.69%, respectively. Edelweiss Discovery Fund holds 10.53%, while ValueQuest S.C.A.L.E Fund commands 8.92%. 
Financially, Rentomojo has continued to grow while remaining profitable. Its revenue from operations rose 45.5% year-on-year to Rs 387 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 266 crore in FY25. Profit after tax jumped 142% to R 104.2 crore from Rs 43.1 crore in the previous fiscal.
As of March 2026, Rentomojo had 2.54 lakh live subscribers across 29 cities. The company operates through 20 warehouses and 82 experience stores.

Leanwatts plans to expand into public charging solutions, rectifiers, power modules, hybrid inverters, and other power conversion applications.
The company is also working with engineering institutions on industry-oriented R&D programmes. It is targeting an annualised revenue run-rate of around Rs 60 crore ($6.25 million) by March 2027, driven by the expansion of its existing EV programmes and new applications.
Leanwatts competes with players such as Neenjas Electric, Dynolt, and IPEC.
The power electronics segment in India has attracted funding in recent years, with startups developing products across EV charging, power conversion, inverters, and related applications. title: Ultrahuman raises $70 Mn from Qualcomm, Alpha Wave, Nexus and others
summary:
Wearable tech startup Ultrahuman has raised $70 million in a funding round led by Qualcomm Ventures, with participation from Labcorp, Alpha Wave, Blume Ventures, Nexus Venture Partners, Alteria and other investors.
The Bengaluru-based company said it will use the capital for product development across sensing, AI, miniaturised electronics, health algorithms, clinical science and research.
Entrackr exclusively reported about the round on Tuesday based on Ultrahuman’s regulatory filings.
Entrackr’s earlier estimates pegged the company’s post-money valuation at around $363 million, a 65% jump from its previous Series B valuation. Ultrahuman had previously raised $35 million in Series B funding and $17.5 million in Series A funding in October 2022.
Ultrahuman said it plans to evolve from a wearable health company into a human-computer interface company built around data from the human body. Its platform combines data from the Ultrahuman Ring, Blood Vision, M1/M2 Live continuous glucose monitoring, Ultrahuman Home and Jade AI system. These products track physiological, biochemical, metabolic and environmental data.
The company has also added research initiatives such as Pulsomics, an opt-in platform that allows Ring users to participate in health studies. Its current programmes focus on sleep, VO₂ Max and glucose metabolism. Other features include AFib Detection, Cycle & Ovulation Pro and cardiovascular fitness age, along with PowerPlugs for additional health-related capabilities.
Ultrahuman reported Rs 565 crore in revenue and Rs 73 crore profit after tax in FY25. The company had projected revenue of around Rs 1,000 crore for FY26 as it looked to expand further in international markets.
Ultrahuman was founded by Mohit Kumar and Vatsal Singhal, who sold their logistics startup Runnr to Zomato in 2017.

title: SoftBank trims Meesho stake through Rs 1,650 Cr block deal
summary:
Japanese investment giant SoftBank has sold 8 crore shares of e-commerce platform Meesho for around Rs 1,650.4 crore through a block deal on Thursday on NSE.
According to stock exchange data, SoftBank’s investment vehicle SVF II Meerkat (DE) LLC sold the shares at Rs 206.30 apiece. The transaction represents around 1.73% stake in Meesho.
The shares were picked up by a mix of institutional investors, including Societe Generale - ODI and Motilal Oswal Large and Midcap Fund. Other buyers included funds managed by Fidelity, Franklin Templeton and Manulife, along with Goldman Sachs Bank Europe, HDFC Standard Life Insurance, Bajaj Allianz Life Insurance, Canara Robeco Mutual Fund, Bank of America Securities and other institutional investors.
SVF II Meerkat held an 8.60% stake in Meesho as of June 2026. If the entire 8 crore shares sold in Thursday’s transaction came from the SoftBank entity, its holding would fall to around 6.87%.
The exit adds to SoftBank’s recent sell-offs in listed Indian technology companies. In August, SoftBank sold another Rs 2,888 crore worth of Lenskart shares through a block deal, following a Rs 2,873 crore sale in June. 
This transaction comes shortly after a strong month of secondary market activity in Indian new-age companies. In August, investors executed 17 block and bulk deals worth Rs 26,337 crore ($2.77 billion) across 12 companies, including Meesho, Groww, Eternal and Lenskart. Meesho alone saw early investors offload Rs 1,949 crore worth of shares through a block deal, followed by Y Combinator’s Rs 970 crore stake sale.
In Q1 FY27, Meesho’s operating revenue grew 48% year-on-year to Rs 3,713 crore, while its net loss narrowed 54% to Rs 133 crore from Rs 289 crore in the year-ago quarter.
At the end of Thursday’ trading session, Meesho's shares closed at Rs 209.74, taking the company's market capitalization to Rs 96,983 crore (around $10.2 billion).

title: Slice raises $100 Mn at $450 Mn valuation: Report
summary:
Digital banking startup Slice has reportedly raised $100 million in a fresh funding round at a valuation of around $450 million.
According to a Moneycontrol report, the round was led by Indian wealth management platform Neo Wealth, with participation from Japan-based Kado Global, US-based Moore Strategic Ventures, and Dhan-parent Raise Financial, among other investors.
The latest round represents a sharp decline in Slice’s valuation from its peak of $1.5 billion, when the Bengaluru-based fintech secured $50 million in a Series C round led by existing backer Tiger Global, with participation from Moore Strategic Ventures and Insight Partners. The firm attained unicorn status with a $200 million Series B round in November 2021.
According to its filing with the Registrar of Companies (RoC), Slice’s board has approved the issuance of 40,347 compulsory convertible debentures (CCDs) worth Rs 403.47 crore ($42.5 million). The proposed allotment includes Rs 106 crore from Moore Strategic Ventures, Rs 95 crore from Kado Global, and Rs 44 crore each from Neo Secondaries Fund and Blume Ventures. Other proposed allottees include Raise Financial, the parent company of Dhan, DSP Investment, and several angel investors.
In addition, the board approved the issuance of partly paid-up shares worth Rs 81.5 crore to Neo Wealth.
According to sources, the $100 million funding included both primary and secondary transactions.
The fresh capital comes at a time when Slice has turned profitable following its transition into a digital bank. The company reported a net profit of Rs 48.4 crore in FY26, compared with a loss of Rs 217 crore in FY25. It has carried the momentum into FY27, with a net profit of Rs 50.9 crore in the first quarter.
Slice’s total income rose 38.6% year-on-year to Rs 413.8 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 298.6 crore in the year-ago period. On a sequential basis, income grew 3.5% from Rs 399.7 crore in Q4 FY26.
In August, Slice also strengthened its board by appointing Samir Sawhney as executive director and Ramesh Kumar as independent director. While both appointments were approved by the company’s board, the Reserve Bank of India approved Sawhney’s appointment as executive director.

title: Cradlewise raises $12 Mn in Series A round led by 3one4 Capital, Prudent Investment
summary:
Consumer health and wellness company Cradlewise has raised $12 million in a Series A funding round led by 3one4 Capital and Prudent Investment Management.
With this round, Cradlewise has raised a total of $26 million to date, backed by Sean O’Sullivan Ventures, Footwork VC, Charles River Ventures, 3one4 Capital, and Prudent Investment Management.
The company will use the fresh capital for growth, channel expansion, product R&D, and geographic expansion, Cradlewise said in a press release.
Founded in 2019 by Radhika Patil and Bharath Patil, Cradlewise is an AI-first consumer tech company that makes smart cribs designed to soothe babies and help improve family sleep.
The company’s AI-enabled cribs use sensors to track movement, sound, sleep state, and other contextual signals. Its system uses this data to predict when a baby is likely to wake up and intervene before the baby fully wakes.
Cradlewise claims its technology can save parents up to two hours of effort each day. The company has patents covering its hardware and sensing systems and says its models are trained on more than 75 million hours of sleep data.
The company also operates an integrated manufacturing facility in Pune, which can produce, test, and pack thousands of cribs each month. This gives Cradlewise greater control over quality, product development, and costs, it said.
Cradlewise’s smart sleep system combines a crib, contactless monitoring, adaptive motion, and a connected app to detect early signs of stirring and help babies settle before fully waking.
The company is targeting the growing intersection of consumer technology, AI, and parenting, with its products aimed at addressing challenges around infant sleep and parental fatigue.

title: ABP Education leads seed round in edtech platform YoLearn.ai
summary:
Voice-first AI tutoring platform YoLearn.ai has raised an undisclosed amount in a seed funding round led by ABP Education, the education arm of ABP Group.
Prior to this, the Noida-based startup had raised $500,000 in a pre-seed funding round at a valuation of $5 million. The round was co-led by DataAlpha.ai and White Swan Global, with participation from a group of angel investors.
Along with the funding, ABP Education will support YoLearn.ai with content, marketing and distribution as the startup looks to provide personalised AI tutoring to K-12 students in India.
As part of the partnership, ABP Group companies Headword Publishing and KIPS Learning will work with YoLearn.ai to convert their school books into content-aligned AI tutors through Headword.ai and kipslearning.ai. The tutors will be accessible through the books students use in classrooms.
The partnership covers a combined network of around 25,000 schools, with potential access to nearly 100 million learners. The partners aim to reach 150 million students and train more than 1.5 lakh teachers in AI-enabled classroom instruction, with a longer-term goal of providing personalized AI learning to 250 million K-12 students in India.
Founded in January 2025 by Kirti Prakash Mishra, YoLearn.ai allows students to scan a code in a textbook and interact with an AI tutor through voice. The platform supports English, Hindi and other regional languages, covering 22 Indian languages.
The AI tutor provides voice-based answers, diagrams and step-by-step solutions through an interactive sketchpad. It also offers practice tests, evaluates responses based on board exam marking patterns, predicts scores and provides parents with updates. The platform supports CBSE, ICSE and state boards.
YoLearn.ai also offers teachers a Co-Teacher Avatar configured to their teaching style, along with more than 50 AI-assisted tools for lesson planning, worksheets, homework, assessments, quizzes and classroom presentations. School administrators can access dashboards covering learning outcomes, areas of weakness, usage and student progress.
The startup competes with players such as SiglQ.AI, Fermi.AI, Arivihan.AI, CK-12, MagicSchool.AI and Lytmus.AI.

title: Ola Electric to consider another fundraise amid market share pressure
summary:
Ola Electric Mobility is looking to raise fresh capital, just three months after raising Rs 780 crore through a qualified institutional placement, according to a disclosure sourced from its stock exchange filing. 
The fresh fundraise comes as the electric two-wheeler maker faces pressure on multiple fronts, including falling market share, mounting customer complaints and a declining share price and market capitalisation.
The company has scheduled a board meeting on September 5, 2026, to consider and approve a proposal to raise funds through the issuance of equity shares or other eligible securities.
According to the regulatory filing, the proposed fundraise could be undertaken through multiple routes, including a private placement, QIP, preferential issue or any other permissible method, subject to regulatory and shareholder approvals. Importantly,  Ola Electric has not disclosed the size of the proposed fundraise.
The development comes shortly after the company raised Rs 780 crore through a QIP in June. Ola allotted around 21.76 crore shares at Rs 35.86 each to qualified institutional buyers.
The fresh capital push comes at a challenging phase for Ola Electric, as it works to improve its financial performance while scaling its vertically integrated EV and battery manufacturing operations. Meanwhile, The company’s scale fell down although its losses improve in the last quarter
In Q1 FY27, Ola Electric’s consolidated revenue from operations fell 45% year-on-year to Rs 455 crore, while its net loss narrowed to Rs 336 crore from Rs 428 crore in the year-ago period. Its vehicle registrations in the month of July were at 13,170 with a market share of 6.8%
The company has also been expanding its battery-cell manufacturing capabilities and recently secured a Rs 95.81 crore incentive under the government’s PLI-Auto scheme for FY27.

title: Bluehill VC leads Rs 10.2 Cr seed round in Makr Microsystems
summary:
Bengaluru-based semiconductor metrology startup Makr Microsystems has raised Rs 10.2 crore in a seed round led by frontier-tech VC firm Bluehill VC, with participation from Artha Venture Fund.
Founded by Ashwin Lal, Makr is developing nanoscale 3D subsurface metrology technology that allows chipmakers to see and measure hidden structures and defects beneath semiconductor surfaces without damaging the chip. 
Its technology combines Acoustic Atomic Force Microscopy (AAFM), optical tomography and 3D data analytics.
The proceeds will be used for technology development, customer validation and commercialisation. Its initial applications include advanced packaging, hybrid bonding, buried interfaces, chiplet interconnects and defect detection.
Bluehill VC claims Makr fits its focus on backing deeptech companies solving difficult problems in critical technology sectors. The fund recently closed its maiden fund at Rs 400 crore.
Makr plans to build globally relevant semiconductor equipment and technology from India as chip architectures become increasingly complex and more manufacturing processes move into three-dimensional structures.

title: Uber to lay off 200–250 employees in India amid global restructuring: Report
summary:
Uber is set to lay off around 200–250 employees in India as part of a global restructuring aimed at simplifying its organisational structure and reducing management layers, according to an ET report. The India cuts are expected to affect teams across its People and Earners organisations.
Globally, Uber is eliminating around 3,300 roles, or roughly 10% of its workforce, in its largest workforce reduction since the Covid-19 pandemic. The restructuring will involve consolidating teams and reducing management layers as Uber reallocates resources towards its mobility, delivery and autonomous vehicle businesses.
The move comes as Uber looks to streamline its organisation after years of expansion. CEO Dara Khosrowshahi has said the company’s growth has led to additional management layers, fragmented ownership and teams that no longer align with its current scale.
The India layoffs reportedly include some engineers working on Uber’s internal recruitment platform. Employees have received layoff communications, with more notifications expected, the report said.
Commenting on the development, an Uber spokesperson said, “Globally, we are making organizational changes to remove layers so we can move faster. As part of these changes, we will be saying goodbye to some valued team members in India, whom we will support through this transition. Our commitment to India as a key market, and our ambition to innovate locally for riders and drivers, remain unchanged - in fact, we are expanding India’s strategic footprint by strengthening our regional operations here to drive our mobility business across Asia-Pacific.”
However, the spokesperson did not disclose the exact number of employees in India impacted by the layoffs.
Uber is also focusing on autonomous mobility and robotaxis while continuing to invest in its core ride-hailing and delivery businesses. The company has also been using AI to automate operations and lower costs. In July 2026, Uber cut around 10% of its customer service workforce as it expanded the use of AI in support operations.

title: D2C brand Plum’s revenue crosses Rs 500 Cr in FY26; profit doubles
summary:
The D2C beauty and personal care space is seeing more activity from larger consumer companies, as established digital-first brands increasingly become acquisition targets. Against this backdrop, Bengaluru-based Plum reported a 28% increase in revenue to cross Rs 500 crore in FY26, while its profit nearly doubled.
Plum’s revenue from operations rose 28% year-on-year to Rs 515 crore in FY26 from Rs 402 crore in FY25, according to its financial statements sourced from the Registrar of Companies (RoC). 

Founded in 2013, Plum sells skincare, bodycare, fragrances, haircare and gifting products through its own website as well as third-party e-commerce platforms such as Amazon, Nykaa and Flipkart. 
Revenue from product sales continued to be the company’s only operating revenue stream during the year. Besides its core operations, Plum earned Rs 14.3 crore from interest income and gains on mutual fund investments, taking its total income to Rs 529.3 crore in FY26.
Plum’s spending remained heavily skewed towards customer acquisition and production costs in FY26. Advertising and promotional expenses rose more than 32% year-on-year to Rs 184.4 crore, making it the company’s largest expense during the fiscal. The cost of materials consumed also climbed 28% to Rs 184.4 crore, while employee benefit expenses increased 12% to Rs 47.6 crore.
Apart from these major cost heads, Plum incurred expenses on storage, commissions, transportation, legal services and other operational overheads. Overall, these expenses took the company’s total expenditure to Rs 481 crore in FY26.
Plum’s faster revenue growth helped improve its profitability in FY26, with profit nearly doubling to Rs 49 crore from Rs 25 crore in FY25. For every rupee of operating revenue, the company spent Rs 0.93 during the year.
Plum’s improved bottom line was also reflected in its key profitability metrics. Its EBITDA margin stood at 8.12% in FY26, while ROCE improved to 13.2%. The company ended the fiscal with Rs 305.6 crore in current assets, of which Rs 92 crore was held in cash and bank balances.

Plum has raised over $50 million across multiple funding rounds. Its largest fundraise came in March 2022, when the company secured $35 million in a Series C round led by A91 Partners, with participation from existing investors Unilever Ventures and Faering Capital. 
In India’s competitive D2C beauty market, Plum competes with brands such as Juicy Chemistry, WOW Skin Science, Mamaearth and SUGAR Cosmetics, among others.
India’s D2C beauty and wellness space has seen a spate of deals, as large consumer companies look to add established digital-first brands to their portfolios. Hindustan Unilever Limited acquired 90.5% stake in Minimalist at a pre-money valuation of Rs 2,955 crore, while Honasa Consumer acquired The Derma Co as part of its expansion in the beauty and personal care segment. More recently, L’Oréal’s reported acquisition of Innovist has further highlighted the growing interest from large strategic players in India’s D2C beauty market.

title: Aakash struggles to break free from Byju's era as topline stagnates for three years
summary:
When Byju’s acquired Aakash Educational Services (AESL) for around $950 million in 2021, the test-prep chain was one of the key pieces of its offline expansion strategy. The idea was to combine Aakash’s classroom network and test-prep expertise with Byju’s technology and reach.
Aakash did see a sharp jump in revenue after the acquisition. Its operating revenue rose 44.6% to Rs 1,421 crore in FY22 from Rs 983 crore in FY21. The company then continued to expand its centre network and student base.
By March 2023, Aakash was expecting to close FY23 with around Rs 3,000 crore in revenue. At the time, it had expanded to 320 centres and had more than 4 lakh students. However, the company eventually reported operating revenue of Rs 2,399 crore for the year.
Byju’s raised the bar further a few months later. In June 2023, while announcing plans to take Aakash public by mid-2024, the company said AESL was on track to clock Rs 4,000 crore in revenue and Rs 900 crore in EBITDA in FY24. The IPO, it was largely expected, would provide enough of a liquidity event for Byju’s to plan the next stage of its expansion without diluting any further equity. 
As it turned out, that target  too remained out of reach.
Aakash’s operating revenue increased marginally to Rs 2,438 crore in FY24, leaving it more than Rs 1,500 crore short of the revenue figure projected by Byju’s. Byju’s deepening financial crisis also scuttled IPO hopes as well.

The slowdown became more visible in the following years. Aakash’s revenue declined 16.7% to Rs 2,032 crore in FY25. In FY26, the business managed only a marginal recovery, with revenue from operations rising to Rs 2,041 crore.
Profitability also came under pressure. Aakash’s EBITDA dropped 65% to Rs 15.3 crore in FY26 from Rs 43.3 crore in FY25.
The numbers show how sharply the growth story has changed. Aakash went from Rs 983 crore in revenue in FY21 to Rs 1,421 crore in FY22 and Rs 2,399 crore in FY23. But since then, it has struggled to move beyond the Rs 2,400-crore mark.
Five years after the Byju’s acquisition, Aakash is now reporting less than half of the Rs 4,000 crore revenue that Byju’s had projected for FY24.
The acquisition did help Aakash scale rapidly in its initial years. But the aggressive growth that followed those early gains has not materialised. Instead, the company has spent the last two financial years without making a decisive break from the Rs 2,000-crore revenue mark, while profitability has weakened further.
Following Manipal’s acquisition of a controlling stake, the group now holds around 73% of Aakash Educational Services. Meanwhile, Byju’s stake has fallen to 13.74%, while Bisy Philip holds 5.16% in the company. During the fiscal year ended March 2026, Aakash founder JC Chaudhry completely exited the company. Chaudhry exit might leave the Manipal installed management with a blank slate to run the firm, but it remains to be seen if it can deliver, even though an impact in FY27 continues to look unlikely.

title: Alpha Wave sells almost entire Pine Labs stake in Rs 550 Cr block deal
summary:
Global investment firm Alpha Wave has exited almost its entire stake in fintech company Pine Labs through a Rs 550 crore block deal on Wednesday.
According to exchange data, Alpha Wave sold 3.54 crore shares, representing a 3.11% stake, at Rs 155.10 apiece in a block deal worth around Rs 550 crore.
The shares were picked up by a group of institutional investors, led by ICICI Prudential Life Insurance Company, which acquired 1.03 crore shares worth around Rs 160 crore.
Other buyers included Societe Generale, Edelweiss Mutual Fund, Goldman Sachs Investments Mauritius, Viridian Asia Opportunities Master Fund, Integrated Core Strategies, JM Financial Mutual Fund, Morgan Stanley Asia Singapore and Norges Bank.
Following the transaction, Alpha Wave will be left with only 4.85 lakh shares in Pine Labs, a fraction of its earlier holding.
The exit comes as Alpha Wave has been actively monetising its positions in Indian technology companies. In June, the investor exited its entire 1.93% stake in Delhivery through open-market transactions for around Rs 665 crore. It has also sold stake in Lenskart, including a 2.46% stake sale in May and further shares worth Rs 1,857 crore in August. Alpha Wave also exited Aye Finance through a Rs 322 crore block deal.
Financially, Pine Labs reported a 20% year-on-year growth in operating scale to Rs 737 crore in Q1 FY26, while its profit jumped fourfold to Rs 20 crore during the quarter.
At the end of Wednesday’s trading session, Pine Labs’ shares closed at Rs 162.3, giving the company total market capitalization of Rs 18,785 crore or nearly $2 billion.

title: Adobe picks up AI marketing startup Rilo in second India acquisition
summary:
Adobe has picked up India based marketing intelligence startup Rilo in a deal involving the licensing of its technology and acquisition of its team. This is Adobe’s second acquisition from India.
The terms of the transaction were not disclosed.
Co founded in 2025 by Georgi Boby and Dhruv Jaglan, Rilo built AI powered tools for go to market teams to automate marketing and sales workflows. The startup had raised $1 million from Peak XV Partners, DeVC and Day Zero Ventures at a valuation of $10 million.
As part of the deal, Adobe is expected to integrate some of Rilo’s intellectual property and onboard its six member team. Rilo’s existing investors are also expected to receive an exit.
Following the acquisition, Rilo will shut down its platform and its products will no longer be available to existing customers.
Rilo’s platform helped teams create customised workflows for competitor intelligence, content repurposing and distribution, and sales call analysis. It also allowed users to build custom AI workflows.
The acquisition comes as companies increasingly use AI to automate marketing and sales tasks. Rilo’s technology could complement Adobe’s existing marketing and customer experience products.
The Rilo deal follows Adobe’s acquisition of AI video creation startup Rephrase.ai in 2023, its first acquisition from India.
In 2025, Adobe also announced plans to acquire SEO optimisation platform Semrush for $1.9 billion.

title: AI content creator platform Creedom raises seed round
summary:
Creedom, an AI growth coach for content creators, has raised Rs 4.1 crore in a seed funding round at a valuation of Rs 42 crore. The round was led by Leigh Hopkins, Raghunandan G, Ravi Iyer, and Kartheeswaran KK, cofounder and CEO of Ninjacart.
The round also saw participation from Raghu Nathan Sethuraman, Senthil Kumar T P and Govindaswamy Megavarnan through Startup Singam.
The fresh funds will be used for product development for Indian creators, expansion into the US and further development of its AI capabilities, Creedom said in a press release.
Founded by Naveen Murugan, Naveen Sowriraj and Aswin Dhananjai, Creedom connects to creators’ Instagram and YouTube accounts and analyses their content and performance data. Its platform identifies trends, recommends what creators should post next and provides insights into why specific content performed well or poorly.
The company delivers these insights through Cree, its AI companion, which allows creators to interact with their performance data through conversations instead of navigating complex dashboards.
Creedom said it has reached more than 1.5 lakh creators through its earlier learning platform before rebuilding its offering around personalised content insights. The startup currently works with creators across India and the US.
In December 2025, Creedom became an Official Meta Business Partner and a YouTube Official Partner. The partnerships allow it to access verified account-level performance data through approved interfaces.
The creator economy has continued to attract funding in India. Influish raised a pre-seed round at a Rs 25 crore valuation in June, while TrueFan AI raised $10 million in Series A funding led by Baring Private Equity Partners India and Z3Partners.
Creator-commerce platforms such as Wishlink and LehLah have also raised funding, while Tring focuses on personalised interactions between celebrities, creators and their audiences.
Adobe’s 2026 India creator survey found that 96% of Indian creators using creative AI said it had accelerated their business or audience growth, while 85% said AI was integrated into or essential to their workflow.

title: Flipkart enters microdrama space with short form content on app
summary:
Walmart-owned Flipkart has launched a micro drama offering on its mobile app, adding short form entertainment content to its ecommerce platform.
Entrackr has seen the micro drama section live on the Flipkart app. The company has added a Play tab to the bottom navigation bar. It includes Explore for creator content and Drama for micro dramas.
The Drama section features titles such as CEO Se Romeo, Contract Marriage, Boss Bahu, Ek Ladki Do Insaan, Elayichi, L, KHEER, Mr Aditi, Nakli Pati Asli Crorepati and Ishq Ibadat. The content is available across genres such as drama, action and comedy.
The app also features performances from actors such as Anupam Kher, Rasika Dugal and Mandira Bedi, among others. Flipkart describes the offering as short stories designed for users to watch during brief gaps in their day.
The micro drama offering is currently available on the Flipkart mobile app. Users can access it through the Play icon and select the Drama section.
Moneycontrol, which first reported the development, said Flipkart has partnered with Terribly Tiny Tales (TTT), Pratilipi and others to produce content. The report also said Flipkart would feature content from Pinkvilla, which it acquired in 2025.
Flipkart’s entry comes amid growing competition in India’s micro drama market. Kuku Technologies’ Kuku TV, ShareChat’s Quick TV, EloElo’s StoryTV and EloTV are among the direct competitors. title: Investors cash out over $2.77 Bn from Indian tech stocks in August
summary:
Indian new-age companies saw substantial secondary market activity in August, with 17 block and bulk deals worth Rs 26,337 crore or $2.77 billion across 12 companies.
The deals were largely led by early-stage investors and promoters offloading their holdings, while mutual funds, insurers and global institutional investors emerged as key buyers.
Lenskart accounted for the largest share at Rs 7,445 crore across three deals. In the wearable firm, SoftBank sold shares worth Rs 2,888 crore, while Alpha Wave offloaded Rs 1,857 crore. In another Rs 2,700 crore block deal, BNP Paribas Financial Markets and Societe Generale sold shares, with most of the stake picked up by BlackRock. The transactions saw participation from institutional investors including Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, ICICI Prudential and SBI Mutual Fund. Overall, institutional investors have offloaded around Rs 14,200 crore, or $1.5 billion, in Lenskart shares over the last few months.”
Paytm followed with two transactions worth nearly Rs 4,986 crore. SAIF Partners and Elevation Capital sold a combined 2.33% stake in One97 Communications for Rs 2,037 crore. Vijay Shekhar Sharma-backed Resilient Asset Management later offloaded a 3% stake for Rs 2,949 crore. SBI Mutual Fund was among the largest buyers in the latter transaction.
Groww also saw two large investor exits worth Rs 3,649 crore. Y Combinator sold shares worth Rs 1,435 crore, offloading its 1.2% stake, while Ribbit Capital sold shares worth Rs 2,217 crore. The transactions came as Groww continued to lead the stockbroking space with 1.31 crore active users and a 28.88% market share as of July 2026.

Foodtech and quick commerce platform Eternal also witnessed a Rs 3,265 crore transaction, with BNP Paribas Financial Markets and Millennium Management affiliate Integrated Core Strategies (Asia) offloading nearly 10 crore shares. BNP Paribas sold shares worth Rs 1,671 crore, while Integrated Core Strategies sold Rs 1,594 crore worth of shares.
Meesho witnessed two investor exits worth Rs 2,919 crore. Peak XV Partners and Elevation Capital sold a combined 2.27% stake for Rs 1,949 crore, followed by Y Combinator's Rs 970 crore sale. Several large institutional investors participated in the first transaction, including Societe Generale, Axis Mutual Fund, Fidelity, Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley.
Outside these four companies, Hero MotoCorp acquired a Rs 1,758 crore stake in Ather Energy from GIC, raising its holding in the electric two-wheeler maker to 32.8%. Unlike most transactions during the month, the deal represented strategic buying rather than an investor exit.
PhysicsWallah saw Lightspeed Venture Partners exit its 1.61% stake through a Rs 550 crore deal, with ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund emerging as a key buyer. Urban Company saw Accel and VY Capital sell shares worth Rs 428 crore to SBI Mutual Fund.
Amagi also recorded a Rs 600 crore transaction involving Accel, Trudy Holdings and AVP Fund. Alpha Wave sold its entire stake in Aye Finance for Rs 322 crore, while WeWork Global offloaded a 2.52% stake in WeWork India for Rs 244 crore.
Capillary Technologies' promoter Capillary Technologies Pte Ltd also sold a 4.14% stake for Rs 171 crore.
The August activity points to rising liquidity in India’s listed startup ecosystem, with Paytm, Lenskart, Groww, Eternal and Meesho accounting for nearly Rs 18,999 crore, or about 72% of the total deal value.
The flurry of deals reflected profit booking and strategic partial exits by early and institutional investors, as deeper market liquidity allowed early backers to monetise their holdings while institutional investors provided the demand to absorb these large exits.

title: Exclusive: Sneaker brand Comet raising Rs 99 Cr at over 3X valuation premium
summary:
The competition in India’s new-age sneaker market is heating up, and Comet is raising fresh capital to strengthen its position in the category. The Bengaluru-based footwear brand is set to raise Rs 98.75 crore ($10.2 million) in a round led by new investor Verlinvest, with participation from existing backers Elevation Capital, Nexus Venture Partners and others.
In July 2024, Comet raised Rs 42.3 crore (approximately $5 million) in its Series A round led by Elevation Capital.
The company’s board has approved the issuance of 70,618 Series B compulsorily convertible preference shares (CCPS) and 10 equity shares at an issue price of Rs 13,983 per share to raise the aforementioned amount, according to its regulatory filing.
Verlinvest, the Belgium-based private equity firm, will lead the round with an investment of Rs 61.73 crore, while Elevation Capital and Nexus Ventures will invest Rs 17.90 crore each. UC co-founder Abhiraj Singh Bhal and Bhaane Retail will invest Rs 50 lakh each, while Ajit Mohan will invest Rs 20 lakh.
As per Entrackr’s estimates, the Bengaluru-based company’s valuation will jump 3.2X to around Rs 535 crore ($56 million) from the approximately Rs 167 crore post-money valuation reported after its Series A round in 2024. 
The company plans to deploy the fresh capital towards working capital requirements, capital expenditure and general corporate purposes.
Founded in 2023 by Utkarsh Gupta and Dishant Daryani, Comet is a Bengaluru-based lifestyle sneaker brand offering sneakers and slides for men and women. The brand focuses on India-inspired, fashion-forward designs and primarily operates through its own platform.
Following the allotment, Elevation Capital and Nexus Ventures will hold 19.72% each in Comet, followed by Verlinvest with a 9.48% stake. Abhiraj Singh Bhal and Bhaane Retail Private Limited will hold 0.08% each, while Ajit Mohan will hold 0.03%.
A March Moneycontrol report had earlier said that Comet was in talks to raise Rs 140-150 crore ($15-16 million) in fresh funding.
The company is yet to file its FY26 financials. In FY25, Comet’s revenue jumped nearly 4X to Rs 29 crore, while its loss increased to Rs 4.39 crore. 
Comet is among a growing set of homegrown sneaker brands, alongside Gully Labs, Neeman’s, ARCs and Doc Sneakers. Gully Labs raised Rs 30 crore in January, while Neemans remains one of the better-funded players with around $18 million raised. India’s large footwear market is still dominated by established players, but the shift could mirror luggage, where D2C brands carved out space by building focused, consumer-first propositions. Sneakers could follow a similar trajectory.

The company plans to use the funds to build 100 new compliant and licensed dark stores as it expands from over 12 to more than 50 cities. Founded in 2023 by Saquib Ali, Shashank Rai and Sagar Chauhan, DocPharma operates as a backend supply chain platform for healthcare businesses. Its network of licensed dark stores, DocPharma One SaaS platform, AI powered inventory management and prescription compliant fulfilment infrastructure support more than 30 healthcare and wellness platforms.
The company works with platforms across categories such as e pharmacies, health insurers, corporate wellness, hospitals, D2C wellness and nutraceutical brands, and pet care businesses. It enables these platforms to deliver medicines and healthcare products to consumers without building their own supply chain.
The Bengaluru based startup claims to operate across more than 12 cities and has fulfilled over 800,000 orders, with a fulfilment rate of more than 95%. It said its operations have impacted more than 500,000 lives across India.
DocPharma said its proprietary SaaS platform integrates warehouse management, inventory intelligence, order management and fulfilment into a single operating system. The platform provides real time inventory visibility, routes orders to the nearest compliant fulfilment centre and enables prescription compliant processing.
The funding comes as healthcare supply chain and quick commerce platforms continue to expand in India, with companies looking to combine faster delivery with the regulatory requirements involved in medicine fulfilment.

The round is led by existing investor Sauce VC, with participation from Peak XV Partners, Niveshaay Sambhav Fund, Ayra Ventures and other existing investors.

In February 2024 the company had raised $12 million or Rs 100 crore in a Series B funding round led by Peak XV Partners (formerly Sequoia Capital India).

Founded in 2020 by former Urban Ladder executives Sangeet Agrawal and Navin Parwal, Mokobara is a Bengaluru-based D2C travel and lifestyle brand. The company offers luggage, bags and backpacks, totes, slings, travel accessories and wallets, targeting the premium travel and lifestyle segment.

Following the allotment, Sauce VC will hold a 20.48% stake in Mokobara, followed by Peak XV Partners with 16.76% and Saama Capital with 13.65%. Co-founders Sangeet Agrawal and Navin Parwal will hold 21.46% and 11.25% stakes, respectively.

summary:
Hospitality brand Zostel has launched Zo Selections, a premium hospitality vertical under its parent company Zo World, with its first property opening in Jaipur. The property offers private rooms, jacuzzi suites, common spaces and workstations.
Founded in 2013, Zostel has grown from a 24-bed hostel in Jodhpur to a network of around 5,000 beds across India, Nepal and Thailand. The company said it has recorded more than 5 million journeys across its properties.
Zo Selections targets travellers who have moved beyond hostel dorms but continue to seek social experiences during their stays. The Jaipur property features bonfires, workshops, sundowners and an in-house restaurant, Amaano, which serves Rajasthani cuisine.
The new vertical expands Zostel’s hospitality portfolio, which includes Zostel Plus, Zostel Homes and Zo House. The company plans to open its next Zo Selections property in Gokarna, followed by locations in Mussoorie, Pench and Lonavla.
The launch comes as Zo World expands its hospitality network. Zostel recently opened its 100th property and its first overseas location in Phuket, while the group has also expanded into Europe through Safestay. Zo World is targeting 10,000 beds as it enters the premium hospitality segment.

By creating an AI layer for production, the company seeks to ensure that faster software development does not come at the cost of reliability, customer experience, or trust. This would enable organisations to fully realise the benefits of AI-driven software development.
The Bengaluru-based startup said its platform is being adopted by enterprise customers across India, the UK, the EU, and the US. It plans to strengthen its agentic platform and expand its capabilities as it works towards making AI-led production operations a reality for enterprise technology teams.

The board at Ultrahuman has passed a special resolution to issue 3,623 Series C and 3832 Series C1 compulsorily convertible preference shares at an issue price of Rs 7,79,500 and Rs 7,85,300, respectively, to raise Rs 583 crore (approximately $60 million), according to its regulatory filings sourced from the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

As per the filing, the company plans to use the fresh proceeds for growth, expansion, and other general corporate purposes.
A July ET report also said that Ultrahuman is in talks to raise $60 million.
It’s worth noting that Ultrahuman’s co-founders, Mohit Kumar and Vatsal Singhal, had earlier sold their first startup, Runnr, to Zomato in September 2017. Zomato later leveraged Runnr, which was merged with Mumbai-based TinyOwl, to strengthen its in-house delivery fleet.

title: Rainmatter leads Rs 30 Cr pre-Series A round in Minimac Systems
summary:
Industrial deep-tech company Minimac Systems has raised Rs 30 crore in a pre-Series A funding round led by Rainmatter, the investment firm backed by Zerodha, with participation from other venture capital firms.
The proceeds will be used to advance R&D in miniaturised treatment infrastructure, fleet automation and fluid analytics. The company will also scale its Recycling on Wheels model through regional hubs across major industrial clusters and strengthen its commercial, digital and operational capabilities, Minimac Systems said in a press release.
Founded in 2012 by Anshuman Agrawal, Minimac Systems focuses on lubricant lifecycle management, reliability and circularity. The company develops miniaturised fluid-treatment systems, operates Recycling on Wheels, a mobile on-site lubricant restoration model, and is developing Lubricants as a Service.
India is the world's third-largest lubricant market, consuming more than 5 million tonnes of lubricants and greases annually, while its annual base-oil import bill has crossed $2.7 billion, according to market research cited by the company.
Minimac's platform covers three stages of lubricant management. NanoCircularity monitors lubricant inside machines through condition monitoring, contamination control and fluid-health analytics. MicroCircularity restores recoverable lubricant at industrial plants by removing contaminants, moisture and degradation by-products. MacroCircularity sends lubricant that cannot be restored to registered re-refiners for conversion into re-refined base oil (RRBO).
Its Recycling on Wheels model uses mobile, miniaturised treatment systems with processing capacities ranging from around 10 to 4,000 litres per minute. These systems assess and treat lubricant at industrial sites before returning it to service. The company aims to abate 860 gigagrams of CO₂e emissions by 2034.
Minimac plans to manage the lubricant lifecycle within industrial plants, covering supply, monitoring, restoration, compliance and end-of-life recovery. Its proposed contracts will be based on uptime, fluid health and agreed outcomes rather than product sales alone.
The company claims to have deployed more than 2,500 miniaturised fluid-treatment systems with a combined installed processing capacity of over 300,000 litres per minute. It has worked across more than 2,200 industrial assets and kept over 14 million litres of lubricant in productive use across India and international markets. Its customers include NTPC, Adani Power, JSW Steel and Tata Steel.
The lubricant circularity segment is still niche in India, with startups such as Santosh Petrochemical Innovations and ReVivo's LubeLoop working on used-oil re-refining and resource recovery.
In March 2026, Re Sustainability partnered with Indian Oil Corporation to build a nationwide used-oil collection and recycling ecosystem, with plans to collect 100 KTA of used lubricants and set up a 50–100 KTA re-refining facility.
Adjacent industrial circularity startups are also attracting investor interest. In January 2026, PolyCycl raised a Series A round from Rainmatter for its chemical recycling technology.

title: Unacademy closes UpGrad deal at $200 Mn
summary:
Edtech major Unacademy has closed its acquisition by UpGrad for just over $200 million, marking a 94% decline from its peak valuation of around $3.4 billion in 2021. 
Unacademy co-founder and CEO Gaurav Munjal confirmed the completion of the deal in a post on Tuesday, acknowledging that the company had raised money at its peak but was now being sold at a fraction of that valuation. 
Entrackr had exclusively reported earlier that UpGrad was set to close the acquisition of Unacademy in a deal valued at around Rs 1,955 crore. The transaction was structured as an all-stock deal, with Munjal expected to continue leading Unacademy following the combination.
Interestingly, Munjal said the deal was not driven by a cash crunch. According to him, Unacademy currently has a topline of around Rs 400 crore, with most of its businesses either profitable or near profitable. The company also has around Rs 900 crore in the bank, he added.
According to Munjal, Unacademy had the option to continue independently but chose to combine with UpGrad after discussions with Screwvala and a belief that the merger would create a stronger education ecosystem.
The acquisition gives UpGrad an entry into the online test-preparation segment, including categories such as UPSC, JEE, NEET and GATE. It also adds Unacademy’s educator network and other businesses to UpGrad’s existing higher education, upskilling and study-abroad portfolio.
Munjal also highlighted Unacademy’s broader impact, saying its educators have crossed 10 billion views on YouTube. He added that the company conducted four ESOP buybacks that created liquidity for employees.
While the exit value is far below Unacademy’s peak valuation, Munjal said he remains confident that shareholders can create significant value from the combined business going forward.

title: Deep-tech aerospace startup Alteon raises $2.5 Mn led by Lachy Groom
summary:
Deep-tech aerospace startup Alteon has raised $2.5 million in a pre-seed funding round led by Lachy Groom, with participation from Together Fund.
The round follows a recent flight test in which Alteon’s aircraft demonstrated autonomous flight within a metre of the ocean’s surface. The test helped derisk a key component of the manoeuvre on which the company’s autonomous, high-endurance flight capability relies.
The fresh capital will be used for offshore tests aimed at achieving autonomous dynamic soaring without propulsion. Alteon will also scale its R&D efforts to deploy a fleet of such aircraft over the ocean, the company said in a press release.
Founded in 2025 by Samay Sanghvi, Alteon develops autonomous aircraft designed to fly for months by using dynamic soaring to harvest energy from the atmosphere. The Bengaluru-based startup is building a new class of ultra-high-endurance aircraft that can remain airborne by drawing energy from the environment.
Its autonomous dynamic-soaring vehicles extract energy from wind gradients, similar to albatrosses, to remain airborne for extended periods. A key engineering challenge is enabling the aircraft to perform this manoeuvre autonomously close to the surface of a moving ocean.
Alteon plans to progressively test its ability to harvest energy from wind until the aircraft can sustain flight without propulsion, similar to an albatross.
The company’s aircraft fleets can carry payloads for applications such as mapping weather and ocean conditions, tracking ships and fishing activity, monitoring critical infrastructure, and supporting defence, search and rescue, scientific and industrial operations.
Alteon said its fleets could provide a continuous, real-time layer of capabilities over the ocean at a fraction of the cost of ships, satellites and large offshore installations.
The funding comes as India’s autonomous aircraft ecosystem gains investor interest. Airbound recently raised $37 million in a Series A round to develop lightweight autonomous delivery aircraft.
While dynamic-soaring aviation remains an early and highly specialised segment, recent funding activity points to growing interest in autonomous flight, advanced drones and next-generation aerospace technologies in India.

RemitX operates 32 branches across 16 states and more than 30 cities, including Tier-2 and Tier-3 markets. The acquisition will take Niyo’s physical presence to more than 40 locations across India.
